> 屯。元亨，利貞。勿用有攸往，利建侯。

Hexagram three is the first one that is simply difficult, and that is what the name means.

## 屯 is a sprout pushing up through soil

The oracle-bone form shows a shoot arching up against the ground — 草木破土, bending as it comes out.

And 屯 has two readings in the classics, with two senses.

Read tún, it is to gather, to store (囤).
Read zhūn, it is difficulty, obstruction — 說文: 屯，難也.

The hexagram's name is read zhūn. But its form is the sprouting plant.

The two are not in conflict, and the resolution is the hexagram's whole argument: being born is itself difficult. What is obstructed is not doing something wrong — it is the necessary resistance of the beginning.

## 磐桓 is rooted, not stalled

磐 is a great rock; 桓 is a pillar. 磐桓 is that posture: like a stone pillar, circling in place, not going forward.

The point is precise. 磐桓 is not stagnation. A rock does not move because it is standing on what it stands on; a shoot does not grow because the root is going down.

## 邅 is winding

邅 — to turn back, to be deflected. The road is bent and cannot be taken straight.

Not "he did not go." He could only go around.

## 膏: nourishment that cannot be distributed

膏 is fat, oil, the richness that feeds — by extension, the capacity to nourish.

屯其膏 is that capacity stored inside and unable to be spread out.

Not refusing to give. Unable to reach anyone with it. The hexagram treats this as a condition, not a fault.

## 字: to give birth, and to be promised

六二 女子貞不字.

說文: 字，乳也 — 字 means to give suck, to bear. From "bear" it extends to "be promised in marriage," on the strength of 《禮記·曲禮》 女子許嫁，笄而字.

So 不字 has two historical readings: does not conceive, or is not yet promised.

Both are grammatical. Which one you take decides whether this line is about a season for bearing or a season for marrying. This book takes the second, because the same line ends in 匪寇婚媾 — the context is a marriage, not a birth.

## 經綸: sorting silk

經 is the warp thread in weaving; 綸 is the silk cord of a seal. Together they mean the work of putting a tangle of threads in order: find the end, then lay them one by one.

The 象 applies it to a person in a disordered time: not to leave it alone, and not to cut through it with a blade — to draw the leading threads out and lay them straight.

That is a completely different instruction from "be decisive," and it is the one the hexagram gives.

## Why this follows 乾 and 坤

The first two hexagrams are pure conditions: rising, and bearing.

The third is the first moment where a condition meets resistance — and the 象's response is 建侯: establish the local supports.

Which is the practical content of the whole hexagram. At the beginning, what is needed is not momentum. It is that the ground be organized — a place to stand, a person in charge of it, a structure that will hold while the shoot is still bending.

## A test

Take a thing you started within the last year that feels stuck. Ask whether it is 磐桓 — rooted, and the root still going down — or whether it has no 侯, no local structure holding it. The first is not a problem. The second is.
